findings.text: On four held-out muffled recordings, automatic sound timing raised supported answers from one to three.
findings.label: Answer comparison

findings.text: Topic notes kept the score at three of four and reduced request-time thinking, but one correct answer gained and another was lost.
findings.label: Two examples

findings.text: The thinker saved both listener-confirmed laughs and their topics, then flagged laughter in 7/15 separately annotated excerpts.
findings.label: Independent detection check

cost: On the four held-out recordings, mean request-time thinking fell from 297 tokens with automatic timestamps to 230 with timestamps and topic notes. The four topic-writing calls used another 7,439 generated tokens before the question, including a call that reached its limit without returning a note. Timestamp-only runs used the CPU detector and generated no earlier tokens. The mean saving came from the AMI recording. On ConEC, the topic note left request-time thinking unchanged for one version and added six tokens for the other.
muffled_detection: The bandwidth detector localized 8/8 muffled edits in development and 4/4 held out. It also flagged 1/8 and 0/4 unedited companion excerpts, respectively. Each hit required at least 25% intersection over union with the edit interval. The sound-focused Qwen writer localized 1/8 development edits and flagged muffling on two unedited excerpts. It did not qualify for the held-out muffling comparison. If “posts and talks” is accepted for “posters and talks”, its development answers rise from 1/8 to 2/8.
natural_answers: Audio alone and all four tested note conditions answered both listener examples correctly. The broad notes recorded topics but omitted the laughter twice. The sound-focused notes recorded both the laughter and its topic twice. Mean request-time thinking was 191 tokens for audio alone, 209 for broad notes, 206 for the sound-focused writer, 168 for automatic timing and 259 for automatic timing with topic notes. Two examples cannot establish a latency improvement.

examples.title: A meeting introduction
examples.context: In the second AMI excerpt the group is laughing as a participant asks why someone is looking at them. Before hearing the request, the thinker saved both the speaking turn and its connection to the introductions.
examples.note: Why are you looking at me? · role and animal relation in the project
examples.answer: The laughter occurs in excerpt 2 between 9.5 and 11.5 seconds, during a discussion about the speakers' roles and how their animals relate to the project.

examples.title: Airline miles on the American Express call
examples.context: In the first excerpt, the host hoped to use his Delta miles and said his family would appreciate it. The sound-focused writer identified the speaking turn by its words.
examples.note: I think my family would appreciate that. · Delta miles
examples.answer: The laughter occurred in excerpt 1 between 5.5 and 6.5 seconds while the speaker was discussing using Delta miles and how his family would appreciate them.

examples.title: A note corrected a speaker mix-up
examples.context: In a held-out AMI meeting, the timestamp-only answer called the industrial designer Chloe. The topic note identified her as Katie, and the final answer gave the correct contribution.
examples.note: Katie · presenting about the inter workings of the remote control
examples.answer: She was going to present about the inter workings of the remote control.

examples.title: A note changed a financial term
examples.context: The analyst asked about decremental margins. Given the timestamp alone, the thinker used that term correctly. The topic note changed it to incremental, and the same error appeared in the final answer.
examples.note: Morning, maybe just a first question... · incremental margins and cost synergies phasing
examples.answer: The analyst wanted to understand the phasing of cost synergies through the year and whether the $40-50 million in other cost-out actions would cause incremental margins to narrow.

next: Test a larger collection of naturally occurring sounds. Compare the speaking turn linked by a detector timestamp with the original words. Measure false alerts and whether attaching a short quotation prevents changes to names and technical terms.
laughter_detail: Across both corpora, the thinker flagged 7/15 tagged excerpts and the dedicated detector flagged 8/15. Both overlapped the source time in 3/15. With one second of tolerance, the counts were 5/15 and 7/15. Qwen produced no usable event call on five windows, which remain in the denominators. Its zero alerts on controls therefore include incomplete calls.
